parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A student observes different stars from the Earth.
Give two reasons why some stars appear brighter than others.

markscheme_points.text: brighter star could be closer (to Earth)
brighter star could have a greater luminosity (in the visible wavelengths)

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in astronomy and cosmology that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: brighter star could be closer (to Earth); brighter star could have a greater luminosity (in the visible wavelengths)

The Hubble constant is $2.3 \times 10^{-18}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.

$$\text{distance} = \text{....................................................}\,\mathrm{m}$$
